#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of the Chapter


---


**
¶1.
** There
 are some among us who
 say
 that the
 Divine
 Proce
eding consented
 to the formation
 of a merely
 natural self
hood —
 that it
 w
illed for
 such
 a thing
 to come
 into
 being. They
 reason
 thus
: The
 Divine Infl
ux manif
ested the
 form
 of its
 own order throughout
 the natural mind. The natural
 affections and
 self-derived faculties of
 the external
 mind perceived
 that
 form
,
 and they constructed
 from
 themselves
 an external selfhood in
 its
 im
itation —
 what
 is
 called the
 prop
rial will and
 the proprial understanding
. See
, they
 say, that the Divine w
ills
 this
 to happen,
 for
 it
 revealed
 the
 pattern
 of its own order to the natural aff
ections,
 and they built accordingly
. Had
 the
 Divine not cons
ented to the
 existence
 of human
 self
-consciousness, it would not have unc
overed its form
 before
 the natural faculties, nor
 would they have shaped
 an
 external selfhood in
 its
 likeness.


---


**¶2.**
 Concerning
 the Divine
 Infl
ux:
 when
 it
 descended
 and
 manif
ested the
 form of divine
 order,
 it did not come for
 the purpose
 of revealing itself
 to the natural aff
ections of
 the external
 mind. Rather, it descended
 and
 manifested itself
 throughout
 the natural consciousness
 because
 of its own
 interior
 life and the
 divine
 good
, which is
 its
 offspring
 —
 entr
apped in every
 state
 —
 so
 that it might quick
en that
 life,
 grant
 it
 liberation
, and free
 the
 divine element
 from every bond and every ent
anglement in
 which it is held
 captive and
 const
rained within
 the natural.


---

**¶3.
**
 Observe
 further
: the
 natural
 affections and
 the self-derived faculties,
 having
 no inher
ent form
 or
 ordering
 principle of their own, were
 drawn by
 selfish desire toward
 the form
 of divine
 order. They reflected
 upon themselves and
 perceived
 that nothing
 in
 their
 own
 nature resembled it
. They received
 the impression of that
 form
 into the
 will and into
 the interior
 life.
 Afterward
, they constructed
 from
 themselves an external selfhood in imitation
 of that form
 — the
 proprial will and the proprial understanding
. They
 sealed
 the
 lik
eness of the Divine
 within
 their
 own
 desire
 and
 their
 own thought
. Thus
 they
 produced
 a copy
 by
 im
itation, but they
 did
 not reproduce
 it in truth.
 For
 just
 as any
 image fash
ioned from
 below
 merely
 resembles that
 which
 is
 above
 without
 poss
essing its
 life
, so it
 is
 with this external
 selfhood:
 it was
 p
atterned against
 the form of the Divine, but it
 does
 not part
ake of the
 reality
 it
 imitates.

---

**
¶4.**
 Likewise
 with
 perception
 itself
: although
 it resembles divine understanding in
 out
ward appearance
, it is not repro
duced in truth.


---

**¶5.
** This matter may
 be understood
 thus
: Divine
 Wisdom in
 its pure interior state is
 like
 a noble
 and
 free
 woman dwelling
 within her in
most
 chamber,
 abundant
 in spiritual
 ri
ches and
 heav
enly poss
essions,
 beautiful
 in the
 beauty of truth
,
 and
 virtuous in the mod
esty of innoc
ence. She moves
 in freedom
 and in
 ex
al
ted dignity
. The
 fame of her beauty —
 the
 spl
endor of interior
 truth
 — has spread through
 every province
 of
 the mind. Even
 the highest natural
 affections and
 the most ex
alted fac
ulties of the external mind desire her
 rad
iant appearance
. Yet
 they
 cannot
 reach her, for
 she is hidden within
 the
 interior
 celest
ial state
, conce
aled within the in
most sanctuary
.
 Now
, this
 Wisdom would
 never
 leave
 her
 interior
 dwelling
 and
 desc
end into
 the external and
 natural consciousness —
 she would never
 reveal her face and
 her beauty to the open
 sight
 of all
 fac
ulties —
 except
 for
 the sake
 of her
 beloved:
 the divine
 good held
 captive in the lower
 states.
 This
 Wisdom, upon
 whom no merely
 natural faculty
 has
 ever looked, whose
 face no
 external
 thought
 has ever perceived
, who neither
 desires nor del
ights in out
ward manifest
ation —
 she leaves
 her interior
 chamber and
 comes forth
 into
 the midst of all
 states
 of human
 consciousness so
 that every
 faculty
 may be
hold her.
 The noble aff
ections and the elevated
 faculties,
 and
 even the lowest
 sensory capac
ities and
 serv
ile appet
ites, all
 look
 upon her.

---

**
¶6.** According
 to this lik
eness: so
 too does the Divine Infl
ux desc
end.
 As
 this
 noble
 Wisdom comes
 forth —
 not from
 w
antonness, nor from pride,
 nor from any self-derived impul
se — she
 does
 not
 consent to the outer
 world for
 its
 own sake. She reveals her face and
 her beauty solely
 under
 the comp
ulsion of compass
ionate grief
 for
 her beloved one held
 captive below
.

---

**¶7
.** Now this
 too is how the third
 degree of the
 Divine Proceeding operates
: when it descended
 and displayed
 the
 form of divine order consp
icuously before
 all the faculties of the natural mind
, it did not come so
 that all
 the natural affections and self
-derived powers
 would sculpt an
 external selfhood in its
 likeness. Rather, it came
 because the
 divine
 good
 was dispers
ed and suffering throughout the
 whole
 of the natural creation
 —
 cruc
ified,
 as
 it were, in every
 state of being
 —
 so that it might release
 it
,
 lib
erate it, and rescue it from opp
ression. Yet when the natural affections
 perceived
 the form of divine
 order, they desired
 it selfishly.
 They fashioned from
 themselves the
 prop
rial will and the proprial understanding —
 the
 external
 human
 selfhood — without the consent of the
 Divine
 Itself
.


---

**¶9.
** Understand also this further
 teaching
: just
 as the
 prop
rial will and understanding
 were
 formed
 when
 the natural
 affections shaped
 an external selfhood after
 the
 impression
 of divine order, so too a
 mult
itude of intermediate
 fac
ulties,
 subordin
ate powers
, and lesser
 spiritual
 capac
ities throughout
 every
 level
 of the mind received the stamp
 of that same
 form when
 it was
 revealed
 to
 them. For in the majesty of
 divine
 wisdom
 and in
 the warm
th of divine love, they kind
led with their own
 desire and were overcome
. They burned
 with sel
fish lon
ging —
 as
 a man who ga
zes upon
 the majesty of a beautiful
 count
enance is
 consumed
 not
 by genuine
 love but by the
 fever
 of his
 own
 cr
aving.

---

**¶
10.** So
 it
 is with all
 those
 fac
ulties:
 when they beh
eld
 that
 ma
jestic and beautiful form of
 divine order, they received its
 stamp and impression
. They repro
duced it externally in
 likeness — but
 the
 copy
 they
 made
 was fash
ioned from their
 own substance
, not
 from divine
 life
. And
 not
 only
 in
 the
 higher
 faculties, but the
 impression
 descended
 in
ward even
 to the lowest sensory-natural foundations
 —
 even
 to the dens
est ultim
ates of thought
,
 from
 state
 to state. The stamp
 of that divine
 form
,
 which was manif
ested throughout
 the natural mind, was received and
 im
printed everywhere
,
 leaving
 its trace
 in every degree
.


---

**¶11.
** Now, this unprecedented
 self
hood that was
 generated
 an
ew within
 the natural mind — the
 prop
rial will and the proprial understanding —
 is unlike
 anything
 that existed
 in
 the external
 consciousness
 from
 the beginning. No
 such form had
 appeared
 in the lower
 states before
, because the divine image had never previously
 descended into those
 degrees
.


---

**¶12.
** Not all the formations
 that have
 come
 into being within
 the natural mind were produced
 by the direct impression of divine order upon
 the
 natural aff
ections. Rather
, there are other formations that
 arose
 differently.

---

**¶
13.** One of these
 is a
 m
onstrous falsity within
 the chaotic sens
ory consciousness
 —
 a resid
ue swept
 from
 the general order
 of
 contain
ment —
 which
 the Divine
 as
 Source of all
 spiritual
 life permitted
 to desc
end into the mass
 of natural
-sensory cogn
ition. Its own self
-love and its own reasoning gave
 it defin
ite form.


---

**¶14.
** The second formation
 is one
 that fell further
 into the natural will and made
 the
 mass
 of falsities its gener
ative matrix. Its own perv
erted desire became
 its sh
aping
 principle
. From
 itself alone
 it fashioned its
 own nature
 — which
 is the very
 root and
 origin of spiritual death. When this
 evil rose
 up
 from the mass of falsities, it
 sought to destroy every
 work
 of the
 Divine Life
.
 Immediately there
 was
 sent against it the Inv
incible Divine
 Truth
 —
 the mighty
 doctrine
 of spiritual
 power
. This
 truth
 subj
ugated the evil in the regions
 of spiritual
 obscurity and cold. It
 has
 trampled it
 underfoot and holds
 domin
ion over it until the cons
ummation of the present state.


---

**¶15.**
 The third formation is one whose
 nature descended
 upon
 the
 will separated
 from truth — the
 dry
 ground
 without
 the
 water
 of
 any
 true
 cogn
ition. It generated
 from
 itself a false perception and established itself within
 it.
 This
 is the new
 formation that was fashioned and
 now
 manif
ests in
 the natural
 mind.

---

**¶
16.** According to their essence,
 all
 these
 formations belong to fals
ity and evil.
 Yet
 they did not orig
inate directly
 with
 the ruling
 evil when
 it first
 invaded
 the natural mind
. Rather
, their fashioning came about subsequently
 — they
 are composite states
, mix
tures of good and evil, of
 truth and falsity, that have
 appeared and
 been
 made
 manifest within
 the natural consciousness
.

They reflected upon themselves, that [they] had no [one] like him in their creation. They sealed hi[s im]a[g]e in their heart, within their soul. Afterward[s, they] built it according to his likeness; they formed Adam and [Ev]e. They sealed the image of the exalted one in their [soul].
